title: Sickle cell disease
summary: Sickle cell disease affects haemoglobin, the part of red blood cells that carries oxygen. Red blood cells can become stiff and curved like a sickle, which can block small blood vessels and cause pain, tiredness and infections.
inheritance_plain: It is inherited in an autosomal recessive way: a child is affected only if they get a changed copy of the gene from both parents.
carrier_meaning: A carrier (sickle cell trait, HbAS) has one typical copy and one changed copy. Carriers are healthy and usually have no symptoms. They can pass the changed copy to their children.
disease_meaning: A person with sickle cell disease (for example HbSS) has two changed copies. Care has improved a lot, and many people live full lives with regular treatment from a specialist team.
screening: Premarital and newborn screening can find carriers and affected babies early.
suggested_questions: My uncle has sickle cell disease. Could I be a carrier?

card_summary: Red blood cells change shape, which can cause pain and anaemia. Carriers (sickle cell trait) are usually healthy.
carrier_short: One changed copy. Healthy; no treatment needed. Can pass the copy on.
disease_short: Two changed copies. A lifelong blood condition that needs regular care.
care: Haematology clinics, genetic counselling and family support groups.
